> Review snapshot, 2026-10-30. Physical verdict and catalogue novelty are separate. Supporting compact measurements: [evidence directory](../evidence/377656542/). Original scripts and acquisition records: [batch evidence](../batches/).

# TIC 377656542: CONFIRMED attributed eclipsing system

Forty primary and39secondary fits establish two equal-depth kinds at full3.77777d; stronger half-period search is the expected ambiguity. Pixel apertures recover seven secondary events at44.8–45.7ppt linear or41.4–42.4ppt quadratic. The22.3arcsec capable neighbor is strongly disfavored for every primary. Gaia small eccentricity gives a3.3sigma primary-epoch tension, while period agrees; observed near-half-cycle separation favors a more circular orbit. Coarse fixed-TIC geometry is a poor characterization fit (chi2~4207/121, scale at boundary), not a calibrated radius/eccentricity posterior.

Physical verdict: **CONFIRMED**. Full review: **complete**. Novelty: no target EB match in the current specified archives; limited prior-art coverage, not a claim of discovery priority. Physical EB identification is distinct from component characterization.

**CONFIRMED** target eclipsing system: Forty primary and39secondary fits establish two equal-depth kinds at full3.77777d; stronger half-period search is the expected ambiguity. Pixel apertures recover seven secondary events at44.8–45.7ppt linear or41.4–42.4ppt quadratic. The22.3arcsec capable neighbor is strongly disfavored for every primary. Gaia small eccentricity gives a3.3sigma primary-epoch tension, while period agrees; observed near-half-cycle separation favors a more circular orbit. Coarse fixed-TIC geometry is a poor characterization fit (chi2~4207/121, scale at boundary), not a calibrated radius/eccentricity posterior.
